title: JSON to CSV
description: Convert JSON data to CSV format

instructions.title: How to use JSON to CSV Converter

steps.title: Paste or upload your JSON data
steps.description: Paste JSON directly into the input area or drag and drop a JSON file. The tool accepts JSON arrays of objects, nested JSON structures, and complex data from API responses.

steps.title: Configure CSV options
steps.description: Choose your field delimiter (comma, semicolon, tab), toggle nested object flattening, set custom column headers, and drag-and-drop columns to reorder them to your preference.

steps.title: Preview the CSV output
steps.description: See a live preview of your CSV data as you configure options. Nested JSON keys appear as flattened column names (e.g., user.name, address.city) for spreadsheet compatibility.

steps.title: Download or copy the CSV
steps.description: Click Download CSV to save the file or copy it to clipboard. The output is Excel-compatible and ready for Google Sheets, LibreOffice Calc, or any spreadsheet application.

proTips: Use dot-notation column names (user.name) to identify flattened nested fields
Choose semicolon delimiter if opening in European Excel (uses semicolon by default)
Drag-and-drop columns to set the exact column order before downloading
For deeply nested JSON, flattening creates verbose column names — use custom headers to rename them
If arrays contain objects, each object becomes a separate CSV row
Add UTF-8 BOM option if international characters display incorrectly in Excel
troubleshooting: Invalid JSON: ensure your JSON is valid using a JSON validator before converting
Missing columns: some keys may be nested — enable flattening to expose all fields
Arrays in values: configure array handling to expand, stringify, or ignore array values
Wrong encoding: enable UTF-8 BOM if special characters appear garbled in Excel
Empty CSV: verify your JSON is an array of objects, not a single object or primitive value
